column1: Cream the butter and sugar until light. Add the egg, brandy and vanilla and beat well.
Whisk the flour, salt and baking powder, then add to the butter mixture a little at a time, mixing until well blended.
Wrap and chill the dough at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C) and line baking sheets with parchment.
On a lightly floured board, roll out 1/3 of the dough at a time to about 1/8–1/6 inch thick.
Cut out shapes with cookie cutters and place on the baking sheets.
Bake 10 minutes without letting them brown. Cool completely.
For the icing, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Remove from the heat and stir in the milk.
Gradually whisk in the confectioners' sugar until smooth and lump-free, then add food coloring.
For thicker icing, whisk in more confectioners' sugar 1/4 cup at a time, or chill it 10–15 minutes and stir again.
Dip the cookies in the icing and let harden on racks for a few hours, or in the fridge.
The dough keeps well in the fridge or freezer. The recipe is usually doubled.
